subject: Intermittent 5xx / timeouts from Zephyr9b — customer impact & recovery
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@brightside.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@brightside.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Spike of 5xxs from Zephyr9b — affecting production

Hi Priya,

We started seeing elevated 5xx responses and timeouts from requests routed to Zephyr9b around 08:50 PT this morning. Error rate jumped to ~9% for our /generate endpoint for ~15 minutes and customer requests timed out. We've switched routing to an older model but are still concerned about data/latency impact for our enterprise users.

I can share traces and a sample request id (req_20280701_0812) — attaching a short capture. Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing a platform-side event? Our SRE team needs an ETA for a full remediation or recommended mitigation.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform, Brightside AI

Attachment: brightside_capture_req_0812.json (log snippet)

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen@brightside.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Spike of 5xxs from Zephyr9b — affecting production

Hi Ellen — thanks for the quick heads up and the trace. We're seeing correlated 5xx/error spikes in our telemetry on Zephyr9b identical to the timeframe you noted. I'm escalating to ops and the runtime team immediately.

Immediate actions:
- Routing: we've enabled model fallback for affected routes for customers in the us region (your traffic should be served by Zephyr9b-compat_4 until we confirm stability).
- Triage: Ben is pulling GPU node logs and Marissa is validating request/ctx cache behavior across the affected shard pool.
- Ask: Can you share a sample prompt and the customer org id (if permissible) so we can replay?

I'll send a status update in 30–45 mins. Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

— Priya
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Zephyr9b spike — early findings

Quick notes from infra:
- Scope: elevated 5xxs observed in Zephyr9b serving pool A (us-west-2) between 08:46–09:10 PT. Error type: internal server error / request timeout when request size > 6k tokens.
- Initial correlates: we saw a trend of bigger batched requests hitting quantized kernels that caused memory pressure + KV cache misses leading to OOMs and preemption on a subset of hosts.
- Temporary mitigation applied: we disabled the aggressive tensor-scratch optimization flag on pool A and applied node-level restart for 4 of 48 hosts.
- Customer impact: routing fallback should route customers to Zephyr9b-compat_4 (non-quantized) but some long-context requests still experienced timeouts during the restart window.

Attaching zephyr9b_incident_logs_20280701.zip to the thread.

— Ben

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen@brightside.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Status update: mitigation applied and next steps

Ellen — quick update:
- We've applied the mitigation (disabled the tensor-scratch optimization on the affected pool and restarted the impacted nodes). Error rate for Zephyr9b in us-west-2 dropped back to baseline within ~12 minutes of the change.
- Your account traffic should now be fully routed to the compatibility model. Please confirm if you continue to observe 5xxs — if you do, send over any request ids and we'll prioritize those traces.
- Next steps internally: Marissa will run a focused regression test on long-context quantized workloads and Dylan will schedule a rollout for a safer kernel change window with stricter canary ramp.

We will follow up with a short post-incident summary and proposed configuration changes within 48 hours. Again, sorry for the outage window — we know this impacts your SLAs.

Best,
Priya

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Park <ellen@brightside.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Jul 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and mitigation plan for Zephyr9b 2028-07-01

Hi Ellen,

Thanks for your patience while we completed the initial RCA. Attached is the formal postmortem (rwc_postmortem_zephyr9b_v1.pdf). Key points below:

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-07-01T08:46:00Z — 2028-07-01T09:10:00Z (approx).
- Impact: elevated 5xxs/timeouts for long-context generation (>6k tokens) for customers served from Zephyr9b pool A in us-west-2.
- Customer-surface: Brightside AI observed a ~9% error rate spike during the window (matching Redwood telemetry).

Root cause:
- A recent kernel optimization (tensor-scratch aggressive allocation) interacted poorly with quantized attention kernels under high batch memory pressure. This led to memory fragmentation, transient OOMs, and host-level preemption for a subset of hosts.

Corrective actions (already implemented):
1) Immediate: disabled the tensor-scratch optimization and restarted affected nodes (reduced errors to baseline).
2) Short-term (1–2 weeks): add a long-context regression suite for Zephyr9b quantized kernels and tighten canary ramp thresholds for kernel changes.
3) Medium-term (4–8 weeks): introduce an automatic safe-fallback that bypasses quantized kernels for requests > 5k tokens until we've validated memory behavior.

Compensation / SLA: We understand Brightside has an enterprise SLA. I've looped in Ben from our support team to start a credits review; we'll follow up via the usual procurement channel (ref BR-4721).

Attachments: rwc_postmortem_zephyr9b_v1.pdf (postmortem), zephyr9b_incident_logs_20280701.zip (log bundle).

Open items for Brightside:
- Confirm whether you'd like us to proactively pin your routing to Zephyr9b-compat_4 for the next 30 days or rely on automatic fallback.
- Share any critical request ids we should prioritize for deeper trace reconstructions.

If helpful, we can book a 30-minute call to walk through the postmortem with your SREs tomorrow.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll be tracking regressions closely and will keep you updated on the rollout of the medium-term mitigations.

— Priya
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: rwc_postmortem_zephyr9b_v1.pdf
